elicitation_input.question: Which holiday, which had its first official recognition in 1868, was originally called Decoration Day?

llm_generation.text:
Decoration Day, now known as **Memorial Day**, was first officially observed on May 30, 1868. It was established to honor Union soldiers who died during the Civil War by decorating their graves with flowers—hence the name "Decoration Day."

General John A. Logan, leader of an organization of Union veterans, issued a proclamation calling for this day of remembrance. The date May 30 was chosen because it wasn't the anniversary of any particular battle.

Over time, the holiday evolved to honor all American military personnel who died in service to their country, not just those from the Civil War. The name gradually shifted to "Memorial Day," which became more common after World War I, though "Decoration Day" continued to be used by some for many decades. Memorial Day was officially declared the holiday's name by federal law in 1967, and in 1971 it was set to be observed on the last Monday in May as part of the Uniform Monday Holiday Act.
